compiled_state.description:
## The defect

Every "Gerrit Verified Gate" run reports the `main` tip as its `head_sha`, regardless of which
patchset it actually tested. `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` is dispatched from `main`,
so GitHub stamps the run with the sha the WORKFLOW FILE came from; the job then checks out a
Gerrit patchset ref (`refs/changes/NN/CCCC/P`) via
`lfreleng-actions/checkout-gerrit-change-action`. The `git checkout --force <main sha>` visible
early in the log is the `actions/checkout` prelude, not the subject under test.

The result: `gh run list` / the GitHub API present multiple runs of DIFFERENT patchsets as
though they ran against the SAME commit. Two runs that tested unrelated changes look like a
contradiction:

  run 33894700851  head_sha 5932f4951  -> actually tested refs/changes/92/2592/7  (SUCCESS)
  run 33897128528  head_sha 5932f4951  -> actually tested refs/changes/26/2626/1  (FAILURE)

## Why this is worth fixing rather than just knowing

It reads as a main-is-broken signal when main is fine. In ONE session this trap consumed two
separate investigation cycles: once when a CI monitor was armed against the wrong sha, and
again when an orchestrator read the two runs above as a same-sha divergence and dispatched a
root-cause agent to explain a contradiction that did not exist. The cost is not a one-off
misreading; it is that the cheapest, most obvious way to ask "is main green?" -- list recent
runs on main and look at conclusions -- returns answers about unlanded patchsets.

Anyone reading these runs without opening the logs hits it, human or agent.

## Proposed fix

Set a `run-name:` on the workflow that includes the Gerrit change and patchset number (the
change number is ALREADY an input to the workflow, so no new plumbing is needed). That makes
`gh run list` self-disambiguating without opening any logs.

This is deliberately the cheap fix. Changing what `head_sha` reports is not in our gift -- it
is GitHub's semantics for a `workflow_dispatch` on a branch -- so the fix is to make the
run's own NAME carry the identity that `head_sha` cannot.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 - A Gerrit Verified Gate run's name identifies the change and patchset it tested
      (e.g. contains both the change number and the patchset number), so two runs of different
      patchsets are distinguishable in `gh run list` output alone, with no log inspection.
- [ ] AC2 - The name is derived from the workflow's EXISTING change-number input; no new
      required input is added, and a run triggered without that input still produces a
      well-formed name rather than failing or rendering an empty/`null` fragment.
- [ ] AC3 - A test or documented check pins AC1, so a future edit to the workflow that drops
      the patchset identity from the run name is caught rather than silently regressing.
- [ ] AC4 - Branch-head/non-Gerrit runs of the same workflow (if any) still produce a sensible
      name and are not mislabelled as a patchset run.

## Non-goals

Not attempting to change `head_sha` itself, and not touching gate behaviour or vote casting --
the gate is CORRECT today. It caught the real defect in change 2626 patchset 1 and recorded
`Verified-1`. This ticket is purely about run METADATA legibility, so nothing here should
alter which votes are cast or when.
compiled_state.title: Gerrit Verified Gate runs report main's tip as head_sha regardless of the patchset tested, so gh run list shows unrelated patchsets as same-sha contradictions
